summary: Defines a SIP event package for collecting and reporting quality metrics for VoIP sessions. Information from RTCP-XR and SIP call details is sent from a user agent to a collector.

plainLanguage.summary: After a phone call over the internet, the phone can send a report card about how good the call sounded to a central collector.

questions: what is sip voice quality reporting
what is the vq-rtcpxr event package
what is a sip collector and reporter
what is the application/vq-rtcpxr media type
subtitle: How a phone reports the quality of a VoIP call to a central collector using SIP messages.

tldr.problem: RTCP quality reports normally go to the other endpoint in a call, which makes it hard for an administrator or management system to gather call-quality data in one place.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 6035 defines a SIP event package, vq-rtcpxr, and a media type, application/vq-rtcpxr. A user agent (the reporter) sends text reports of RTCP and RTCP-XR metrics to a collector, preferably in NOTIFY messages after the collector subscribes.
tldr.outcome: A collector can receive session, interval and alert reports for voice calls. The specification covers point-to-point calls only, and the RFC leaves configuration to a separate framework.

today: RFC 6035 is a Proposed Standard, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It builds on SIP event notification (RFC 3265) and the RTCP XR metrics of RFC 3611.

sections.title: Why Report Call Quality Over SIP
sections.content:
Real-time communication over IP uses SIP for signaling and RTP/RTCP for media transport and reporting. RTCP reports usually go to the other endpoints in a session, so collecting performance data centrally is complex. RFC 6035 forwards the data in RTCP XR VoIP metrics reports (RFC 3611) to a central collection server using SIP.

Only a minimal set of parameters is included: the codec type from the SDP offer-answer, burst gap loss density and max gap duration, round-trip delay, and conversational quality as a catch-all for other impairments such as random packet loss and jitter. The RFC notes that RTCP reports are best effort only, so this must be considered in managed networks.

The document defines a new SIP event package, vq-rtcpxr, and a new MIME type, application/vq-rtcpxr. The event package SHOULD be used with SUBSCRIBE/NOTIFY. It MAY also be used with PUBLISH for backward compatibility with some existing implementations.
sections.plainLanguage: Normally the people on a call only tell each other how it sounded. This document lets the phone also tell a central helper, so a technician can find calls that sounded bad.

sections.title: What Call Setups Are Covered
sections.content:
RTP is used in many topologies, and RFC 5117 lists them. This specification supports only the first, point to point. That reflects the VoIP deployments the authors describe as predominantly point to point using unicast, and the state of research on quality.

Reporting quality for a multipart conference or a session through translators and mixers is called an area of research. The mechanism can still be used for centrally mixed conference calls in which each leg is a point-to-point call. A single report may carry several report bodies, for example one per remote endpoint in a multi-party call, or one per segment after call hold or transfer.
sections.plainLanguage: It works well for a call between two phones. Big group calls with lots of mixing in the middle are still being figured out.

sections.title: Reporter, Collector and Delivery Methods
sections.content:
Two roles are defined. The reporter is the SIP user agent involved in a media session, and it measures and reports quality. The collector receives the vq-rtcpxr events and may be a proxy server or another capable entity.

With SUBSCRIBE/NOTIFY, the collector SHALL send a SUBSCRIBE to the reporter, and the reporter SHOULD send reports in NOTIFY messages. The reporter MUST NOT send any vq-rtcpxr events if a collector address has not been configured. The default subscription duration is one hour; durations from minutes to weeks are allowed, and hours or days are RECOMMENDED.

With PUBLISH, a user agent MAY send reports to the collector's address, but this SHOULD NOT be used, in general, on the public Internet. The reporter is RECOMMENDED to send an OPTIONS message first to check that the collector supports PUBLISH. A 501 Not Implemented or 405 Method Not Allowed response means the reporter stops publishing.

For overload avoidance, an overloaded proxy or collector MUST send a 503 Service Unavailable or other 5xx response with a Retry-After time, and reporters MUST respect it. Suggested approaches are one report at the end of each call, interval reports only on problem calls, and at most one alert per call.
sections.plainLanguage: The collector first says, please send me your report cards. The phone then sends one when something worth reporting happens. If the collector is too busy, it says wait, and the phone has to wait.

sections.title: The Three Report Types and Their Format
sections.content:
There are three NOTIFY bodies. A Session report SHOULD be used when a voice media session ends, when media changes (such as a codec change or session fork), or when a session ends because no media packets arrive. It MUST NOT be used at arbitrary points and MUST carry cumulative metrics from the start of the session. An Interval report SHOULD be used for periodic reporting of short windows, which SHOULD NOT overlap. An Alert report MAY be used when voice quality degrades during a session.

The body is a text encoding of RTCP and RTCP-XR statistics, sent as application/vq-rtcpxr. The syntax is given in ABNF. A report begins with a line such as VQSessionReport, VQIntervalReport or VQAlertReport, followed by session information (call ID, local and remote IDs, addresses, group IDs), then LocalMetrics and optionally RemoteMetrics, and optionally a dialog ID.

An alert report adds a metric type, a severity (Warning, Critical or Clear) and a direction (local or remote). Metrics are measured over the interval set by the START and STOP timestamps, which are in UTC with no time zones other than Z. Most parameters are optional, and unknown or inapplicable values are simply left out.
sections.plainLanguage: There are three kinds of report cards: a final one at the end of the call, a quick check during the call, and a warning when things sound bad.

sections.title: The Metrics and Where They Come From
sections.content:
Metrics are grouped into lines in each metrics block: SessionDesc (codec payload type, sample rate, packets per second, frame data), JitterBuffer, PacketLoss, BurstGapLoss, Delay, Signal and QualityEst. Most map directly to fields in the RTCP XR VoIP Metrics block of RFC 3611. Metrics that RFC 3611 gives as an 8-bit fixed-point number are mapped to percentages by dividing by 256 and taking the integer part.

Delay values are in milliseconds. Round-trip delay may be measured as in RFC 3550, and symmetric one-way delay is computed by adding round-trip delay to the local and remote end system delay and dividing by two.

Quality scores include R factors and mean opinion scores (MOS). The range of R is 0-95 for narrowband calls and 0-120 for wideband calls. MOS is on a scale from 1 to 5, where 5 is excellent and 1 is unacceptable. When RFC 3611 reports the value 127, the quality is unavailable and the parameter MUST be omitted. Each estimate can name the algorithm used, and algorithms SHOULD comply with ITU-T P.564 and G.107.
sections.plainLanguage: The report card has lines for how many sound pieces got lost, how shaky the timing was, how loud the voice was, and an overall score from 1 to 5, with 5 being excellent.

sections.title: Worked Examples
sections.content:
The RFC walks through four flows with full messages: an end-of-session report using NOTIFY, a midsession threshold violation using NOTIFY, an end-of-session report using PUBLISH, and an alert report using PUBLISH. In the NOTIFY flows the user agent registers with Allow-Event: vq-rtcpxr, the collector subscribes through the proxy, the call proceeds with RTP and RTCP XR, and the NOTIFY carries the report.

One example report starts VQSessionReport: CallTerm, where CallTerm marks the final report of a session. It includes lines such as PacketLoss:NLR=5.0 JDR=2.0 and Delay:RTD=200 ESD=140 SOWD=200 IAJ=2 MAJ=10. The alert example uses VQAlertReport: Type=NLR Severity=Critical Dir=local.
sections.plainLanguage: The document shows full sample report cards, so builders can copy the shape and see where each number goes.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
RTCP reports can contain sensitive information because they reveal the nature and duration of a session between endpoints. Any third party that wants this information SHOULD be properly authenticated by the SIP user agent using standard SIP mechanisms. The event content MAY be encrypted to ensure confidentiality, using the mechanisms in RFC 3261.

The PUBLISH method also needs care: to protect SIP proxies and the collector, the reporter MUST be configured with the collector address.
sections.plainLanguage: A report card shows who talked and for how long, so only trusted helpers should be allowed to get it.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: The document registers a SIP event package named vq-rtcpxr (type: package) and the media type application/vq-rtcpxr. The media type has no required or optional parameters, uses 7 bit encoding, and its intended usage is COMMON. The IETF is the change controller. The RFC suggests that the SIP configuration framework be used to set up the parameters, with a dataset to be documented separately.
sections.plainLanguage: The authors put the new name and the new kind of message in the official list so nobody else uses the same name.

messages.label: NOTIFY with application/vq-rtcpxr
messages.note: Sent after the session ends, or on a threshold violation.

items.title: Session report
items.text: Cumulative metrics from the start of the session, for when it ends or media changes.

items.title: Interval report
items.text: Periodic reports of short, non-overlapping time windows.

items.title: Alert report
items.text: Sent when quality degrades, with a metric type, severity and direction.
